quickAnswer: Hopedale pairs very old housing with heavy oil use: 33.5% of homes date from 1939 or earlier, the 3rd-highest share of the 50 towns we serve, and 61.9% of occupied homes burn oil. With that much oil, a boiler replacement here can turn on oil versus a heat pump.
body: ## An old median house and very few new ones

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) dates the median Hopedale home to 1962, against 1975 for the middle of the 50 towns we serve. The oldest band is the striking one: 770 of the town's 2,300 housing units (33.5%) went up in 1939 or earlier, which ranks 3rd of 50. At the other end, only 73 units (3.2%) have been built since 2010, 49th of 50. Overall, 57.1% of homes predate 1980, almost exactly the 57.2% of the middle town.

Houses built in 1939 or earlier often have less insulation and more air leakage than newer ones, and an old boiler may sit in a space that does not suit today's equipment. Sizing a new system from the home's heating load, rather than from the nameplate on the old unit, avoids repeating an old mismatch.

Housing types add to the picture. Single-family detached homes are 1,228 of the 2,300 units (53.4%), 45th of 50, and attached townhouses are another 590 (25.7%). The median value of an owner-occupied home is $405,400, which ranks 43rd. Renters occupy 458 households (21.1%), so some heating decisions belong to landlords rather than residents.
## Oil first, utility gas a distant second

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,343 occupied Hopedale homes (61.9%). That is the 8th-highest share among the 50 towns, against 36.5% in the middle town. Utility gas ranks only 41st, so oil is the fuel to think about first whenever a boiler or furnace gives out.

An oil system needs a yearly cleaning and tune-up, and the tank, chimney and burner all age together. When one part fails, it is a reasonable moment to compare a like-for-like oil replacement with a heat pump, which both heats and cools. Which one wins depends on the house, not on a rule of thumb. Details on the heating side are on our [Hopedale heating page](/cities/hopedale/heating-installation-repair).
## Draper looms and a utopian experiment

Hopedale took its name on August 26, 1841, when Adin Ballou and the Practical Christians named the place, and they founded the Hopedale Community in 1842. It went bankrupt in 1856, and Ebenezer and George Draper, loom manufacturers, bought its assets. The town was incorporated in 1886 after separating from Milford. George Draper designed, paid for and built the town hall, made of Milford granite and sandstone and dedicated in 1887.

The Draper Corporation was at its peak the largest maker of textile looms in the United States. Rockwell International acquired the company in 1967, and the Draper factory closed on August 29, 1980. The site has since been demolished and leveled. The Unitarian church was another Draper gift, and the Bancroft Memorial Library came from a superintendent at the plant. Hopedale covers 5.3 square miles, of which 5.2 is land, and the largest body of water is Hopedale Pond near the town center. The town also holds the Parklands, a 275-acre public nature reserve around the pond, designed in 1899 by a firm operated by Frederick Law Olmsted. Wikipedia also places Hopedale in the Blackstone River Valley National Heritage Corridor, with much of the town in the Charles River watershed.
## National Grid and the rebate question

National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company territory list includes Hopedale, so Mass Save heat pump rebates generally reach Hopedale customers, subject to the weatherization conditions and the dates set by the program. The current amounts are on the [heat pump page](/cities/hopedale/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits); terms can change, so confirm at masssave.com.

faq.q: Should I replace my oil boiler in Hopedale with a heat pump?
faq.a: It depends on the house. With 61.9% of occupied homes on oil, the question comes up often. A heat pump can heat and cool, and Mass Save rebates may help, but the home has to be weatherized first. The heating load, assessed before a system is quoted, gives both choices the same footing, and a free written estimate comes before any work starts.

faq.q: Does a very old house change how a new heating system is sized?
faq.a: Yes, it can. With 33.5% of Hopedale homes built in 1939 or earlier, air leakage and insulation vary a great deal from one house to the next. Oversized equipment cycles on and off, and undersized equipment struggles in January. Insulation and air sealing done earlier can also change the answer.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to swap a gas boiler or furnace in Hopedale?
faq.a: Usually. A new gas furnace or boiler normally needs a permit and then an inspection, and only a licensed plumber or gas fitter can file for it. Ask the town's building department what it expects before work starts, and ask whoever will pull the permit whether the job counts as a replacement or a repair.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in a Hopedale rental?
faq.a: The landlord covers the heating bill unless the lease says otherwise, and the State Sanitary Code sets minimum temperatures for rented homes in the heating season. The exact figures are on the heating page. This is general information, not legal advice. A landlord with a failed system can phone (508) 786-8755 day or night.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil leads in Hopedale, yet 430 occupied homes use utility gas and 355 use electricity, so the right repair or replacement varies by house. About one household in five rents, and Massachusetts sets a heat schedule for rented homes.
body: ## The fuels behind the other systems

Oil dominates the town, but the remaining fuels still add up. The ACS 2022 counts 430 occupied homes (19.8%) on utility gas, 355 (16.4%) on electricity and 32 (1.5%) on bottled or tank gas. Electricity ranks 11th of 50 for share, while bottled gas ranks 48th, so propane is a small slice here.

A gas swap is a regulated job. Massachusetts lets only licensed plumbers and gas fitters pull gas permits, and a new gas furnace or boiler normally ends with a final inspection. The town's building department can say what it expects. A home on electric heat can be a candidate for a heat pump instead, and the [heat pump page](/cities/hopedale/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers that path.
## Older plants

Alongside the 770 oldest units, 344 (15.0%) date from 1940 to 1959. A boiler in a house this old may have been replaced already, and the chimney, tank or piping around it can be older than the burner. Rust flakes, weeping fittings and a burner that never quite settles are signs worth acting on before January.
## Rented homes and the heating schedule

Renters live in 458 Hopedale households (21.1%), 19th of 50. Massachusetts sets minimum temperatures for rented homes in the heating season, roughly mid-September to mid-June: 68 F between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m. and 64 F overnight (105 CMR 410.201). Heat is the landlord's cost unless the lease says otherwise. This is general information, not legal advice.
Boilers in rentals tend to fail in cold snaps rather than in October, so for a landlord the repair call is an urgent one.
## Before you replace anything

Hopedale sits about 25 miles southwest of Boston in eastern Massachusetts. Winter equipment has to carry a house through January, and sizing matters more than the label on the box. Mass HVAC assesses the home's heating load, then hands over a free written estimate before work starts. Heating work covers homes and businesses.

faq.q: Who is allowed to pull the gas permit?
faq.a: A licensed plumber or gas fitter, and nobody else in Massachusetts. In Hopedale 430 occupied homes heat with utility gas, and swapping one of those boilers or furnaces normally needs the permit and a final inspection. Ask your installer to name who is filing the permit, so there is no gap between the old unit coming out and the new one running.

faq.q: Is there a number for after-hours heat failures?
faq.a: Yes: (508) 786-8755, any hour, every day, because emergency calls are taken 24/7. A landlord with an oil boiler down in a three- or four-unit building should say how many households are without heat. The fuel, the age of the system and what stopped working are the details that help most.

faq.q: Is propane a common fuel in Hopedale?
faq.a: Not really. Only 32 occupied homes use bottled or tank gas, while oil heats 1,343. Anyone weighing propane against oil or a heat pump should compare the tank, the deliveries and the gas permit that new equipment normally needs, along with how much each fuel costs to run in that particular house.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Hopedale has 1,228 single-family detached homes and 590 attached townhouses, plus a scattering of two-unit and larger buildings. Many older houses were built without central air, so ductless mini-splits are often worth pricing next to a ducted system.
body: ## A town of houses, townhouses and small buildings

According to the ACS 2022, single-family detached homes make up 53.4% of Hopedale's housing units (1,228), well below the 76.7% of the middle town and 45th of 50 for share. Attached townhouses add 590 units (25.7%). Two-unit buildings account for 192 units (8.3%), buildings of three or four units for 98 (4.3%), and buildings of five or more for another 192 (8.3%). Taken together, 21.0% of units sit in multi-unit buildings.

That mix means cooling is not one job. A detached house can often take a ducted central system if the ductwork is suitable, or a set of ductless heads if it is not. A townhouse or an apartment may be limited by where an outdoor unit can go, and the building's rules may matter. Each building sets its own limits.
## Cooling in older buildings

Many older homes were built without central air, and in a town with a median build year of 1962 it is worth asking what ductwork a house really has before assuming a ducted system fits. A mini-split links indoor heads to an outdoor unit through a small hole in the wall, and the same unit can heat. The [heat pump page](/cities/hopedale/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the rebate side.
## Two-family and small buildings

Hopedale has 192 units in two-unit buildings (8.3%) and 98 in buildings of three or four units (4.3%). In a small building the first question is whether one system serves everyone or each household has its own. Ductless heads let each apartment set its own temperature, but who owns the equipment and who pays for the power usually settle the choice.
## Sizing and the summer load

Cooling equipment that is too large satisfies the thermostat before it has removed much moisture, which can leave rooms clammy. Undersized equipment runs and runs without catching up. Sun on the walls, window area and insulation all change the answer. Air conditioning work from Mass HVAC covers both homes and businesses.

faq.q: Can a mini-split cool a Hopedale house without ducts?
faq.a: Yes. Indoor heads connect to an outdoor unit through a refrigerant line and a small wall opening, so no ductwork is needed. The head count follows the layout of the rooms. Hopedale's median house dates to 1962, and a mini-split avoids opening plaster or framing to run ducts where none exist.

faq.q: Is central air or a mini-split better for a townhouse?
faq.a: A townhouse with limited outdoor space may suit ductless heads better, but it depends on the building. Hopedale has 590 attached townhouse units (25.7%), and an association or neighbor wall can limit where an outdoor unit goes. Existing ductwork, if any, tilts the choice toward a central system.

faq.q: Do two-family houses in Hopedale need one cooling system or two?
faq.a: Either can work. One central system can serve both floors, or each unit can have its own system so each household controls its comfort and its bill. Ownership, the existing ductwork and how the electric meters are arranged tend to decide it, and the outdoor equipment still needs a sensible place to sit.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Hopedale is on National Grid's territory list, so Mass Save heat pump rebates generally reach the town once a home is weatherized. With 1,343 oil-heated homes, heat pumps are a live question here, and the amounts for 2026 are below.
body: ## National Grid territory

Because National Grid's Massachusetts Electric Company list names Hopedale, most addresses generally fall under Mass Save. For 2026 the whole-home air source rebate is $2,650 per ton, capped at $8,500 per home, and weatherization has to come first. Hopedale's housing stock makes that first step a real one. Conditions are laid out on the [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits); confirm current terms at masssave.com.
## The weatherization gate against Hopedale's ages

Construction date is the easy route through that gate. A house built in 2000 or later qualifies on age, and Hopedale has 333 of them (14.5%), though only 73 (3.2%) went up since 2010. The rest of the stock is older: 770 units (33.5%) from 1939 or earlier, 344 (15.0%) from 1940 to 1959, 200 (8.7%) from 1960 to 1979 and 653 (28.4%) from 1980 to 1999. For houses in those bands, an energy assessment may be the first step.
## An oil-heavy town looking at electric heat

Fuel oil leads here, and utility gas ranks 41st of 50, so a move away from oil does not usually mean a gas conversion. Electricity already heats 355 homes (16.4%). A heat pump heats and cools from one system, and a ductless mini-split fits a house with no ducts. Some owners keep the boiler for the coldest days. That is a judgment call for each house, made after the heating load is assessed. The [Hopedale page](/cities/hopedale) has the full fuel breakdown.
## Houses, townhouses and heads

Of 2,300 housing units, 1,228 are single-family detached and 590 are attached townhouses. A detached house can take several indoor heads. A townhouse is often limited by where the outdoor unit can sit.

faq.q: Is Hopedale eligible for Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: Hopedale is on National Grid's territory list, so an address here would normally go through Mass Save. Weatherization comes first, the program may revise its terms, and the installer must be on the eligible list. Check masssave.com for the current amounts before you sign a contract or order equipment.

faq.q: How does a house show it is weatherized enough?
faq.a: There are three routes: construction in 2000 or later, an energy assessment calling for under $1,000 of work, or completion of recommendations dated 2013 or later. In a town where a third of the units date from 1939 or earlier, many owners would probably start with the assessment and see which route fits.

faq.q: Can a house on oil go straight to a heat pump?
faq.a: Yes, the old fuel does not bar it. The weatherization test and the 2026 dates still govern the rebate, and the old boiler can stay as a backup if the owner wants one. The tank can be removed or left empty, depending on the house, once the heat pump is carrying the load.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil is Hopedale's leading fuel, and oil systems need a yearly cleaning. Of 2,171 occupied homes, 1,713 are owner-occupied, so a regular tune-up helps those owners decide when to repair and when to replace.
body: ## Mostly owners, some landlords

Of the occupied homes counted in the ACS 2022, 1,713 (78.9%) are owner-occupied and the other 458 are rented. An owner can pick the timing of service. A landlord faces a tighter clock, because a tenant without heat in the cold months cannot wait.
## Fuel by fuel

- **Oil:** burner and heat exchanger cleaned once a year, nozzle and filter replaced, combustion measured.
- **Gas:** burner, flue and controls checked for safety and efficiency.
- **Heat pumps and mini-splits:** coils and filters cleaned, refrigerant side inspected.
- **Electric baseboard:** thermostats and connections looked over.
The details change with the equipment and its age.
## Reading the age of a heating plant

The median Hopedale house dates to 1962, so the boiler or furnace in many of them may have been replaced at least once. A service visit is a good time to catch weeping fittings, rust flakes, a noisy burner or a system that never quite reaches the set temperature. Spotting one early gives an owner months to plan instead of a January emergency.
## Empty houses

Hopedale counts 129 vacant housing units (5.6%), the 10th-highest rate among the 50 towns. Equipment in a house that sits empty still needs its fuel, thermostat and pipes watched through the cold months, and a service visit in the fall is a chance to confirm the heat will come on.
## What owners can do between visits

Change or clean the filter on schedule, check the thermostat batteries and settings before assuming something has failed, and keep leaves and snow off outdoor units. Note the date of each service so the next visit has a history to work from.
## Timing

Book heating work between late summer and the first frost, and cooling checks in spring. A strange sound or smell does not wait for the calendar. Write down the fuel and the equipment's approximate age before you call. For repair and replacement, see the [heating page](/cities/hopedale/heating-installation-repair). Mass HVAC services homes and businesses.

faq.q: Does a Hopedale oil burner need service every year?
faq.a: Annual cleaning is the standard advice for oil systems, best done before the heating season. With 1,343 occupied homes on oil in town, it is a very common job. Skipping it can mean soot build-up, a clogged nozzle and an unplanned breakdown on the first cold night.

faq.q: What belongs on a landlord's pre-winter checklist?
faq.a: A service visit on every boiler or furnace, working thermostats, and a plan for who to call overnight. Massachusetts expects rental heat on a set schedule, so a failure is urgent. Hopedale has 458 rented households, and a small building with one boiler can lose heat for every unit at once. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: When should a heat pump or mini-split be serviced?
faq.a: Filters want attention several times a year, and a fuller cleaning of coils and the condensate drain suits spring or early summer, before cooling starts. Because the same unit heats in winter, a quick check of the outdoor unit for snow and ice is also worth doing between visits.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Hopedale has homes from every era: 28.4% were built from 1980 to 1999 and 8.7% from 1960 to 1979, alongside the town's very old houses. Older houses leak air; tighter ones may need ventilation. Filters, humidity and duct condition matter in both.
body: ## Different eras, different air

According to the ACS 2022, 653 Hopedale housing units (28.4%) were built from 1980 to 1999 and 200 (8.7%) from 1960 to 1979. Houses from the middle of the century and later tend to differ from the oldest ones in how much outdoor air gets in. Many older houses leak air through walls and windows, which can dilute indoor pollutants but also lets in dust, pollen and humidity. Tighter, newer houses may hold moisture and odors longer and often benefit from planned ventilation.
## What to look at

- **Filters:** a clean filter sized for the equipment helps both airflow and dust control. A higher-rated filter is not always the better one if the blower cannot pull air through it.
- **Humidity:** very dry winter air and damp summer air can both be addressed with humidifiers, dehumidifiers or ventilation, depending on the house.
- **Ventilation:** bath and kitchen fans, and in tight homes mechanical ventilation, move stale air out.
- **Ducts:** where a house has ducts, their condition and cleanliness can affect air quality, and whether cleaning helps depends on what is found.
## Shared walls and the oldest houses

Hopedale has 590 attached townhouse units and 192 units in two-unit buildings, so shared walls are common enough to matter. Cooking smells and moisture can travel between neighbors, and a bath fan that vents outdoors helps. The 770 units built in 1939 or earlier can leak air through walls and windows, while the 333 from 2000 or later may be tighter.
## Oil and combustion

Oil heats 1,343 occupied Hopedale homes, so burners and chimneys are part of everyday life. A yearly burner and chimney check matters, because a combustion appliance running badly can put soot or fumes into the house. A carbon monoxide alarm is a basic precaution. A smell or soot near the equipment is a reason to call. Wood is the main heat in 11 homes (0.5%) and brings its own smoke questions.
Mass HVAC handles indoor air quality work for homes and businesses. For the broader picture of Hopedale housing, see the [city page](/cities/hopedale).

faq.q: Does an older house need different air quality equipment?
faq.a: Possibly. Older houses often leak more air, so humidity control and filtration may matter more than ventilation. A tighter house may need mechanical ventilation. Hopedale has both extremes, with 770 units built in 1939 or earlier and 333 from 2000 or later, so the answer depends on which kind of house you have.

faq.q: Is duct cleaning worth doing in Hopedale?
faq.a: Sometimes. Visibly dirty ducts, moisture damage or recent renovation dust are reasons to consider it. Ducts in good condition may only need regular filter changes. Check whether the house has ducts at all before paying for cleaning.

faq.q: What should I do about a musty smell in a townhouse?
faq.a: Start by locating it: a basement corner, a bathroom without a working fan, or a closet on an outside wall. Shared walls and limited airflow can hold moisture, so run exhaust fans, keep vents clear and watch for condensation on windows. If the smell returns, a humidity control or added ventilation may be the right fix.
